failure_modes: the bare phrase 'three questions' in ordinary contexts: the interviewer's own questions, a daily self-improvement ritual, a rune-casting party, a medium's client Q&A
self-directed existential questions in the void ('I asked myself three questions: who am I, where did I come from') - the claim requires a voice asking the experiencer
researcher/host narration listing the questions other NDErs report, or introducing a guest's account in the third person
sermon speculation about what Jesus will ask you when you die
questions the experiencer asked the being, i.e. the reverse direction

best_quote.text: Following several minutes of silence, an unknown voice inquired, "What have you done with your life?" Sadly, I heard myself say, "Nothing. I have wasted the entire 47 years."

life-decision metaphor: a career pivot, leaving a company, 'I'm either going A or B'

the interviewer supplying the phrase and the experiencer only assenting, with no place described

a meditation/surrender threshold rather than a boundary in the other world

best_quote.text: But at the same time, there was something like an invisible fence between me and them. It was something like water, something he could barely see and feel.

failure_modes: anger about something other than the return: a surgical scar and appearance, being late for things, having blamed God

note: this feature is an aftermath emotion rather than a place, so I scored it as 'the anger/grief is reported as the speaker's own on regaining the body'

best_quote.text: I came back and I was very angry that I was back and wished that this call had not come through and broken up my experience.

failure_modes: metaphorical rivers: a 'river of all knowing' (the Akashic records, 2 copies), a raging river used as a simile for incoming love
earthly rivers in biography (the Mohawk River in childhood) and a Nile/Egypt past-scene with reeds and a boat

a creek with a footbridge toward a golden castle - water, but not the uncrossable divide
a commentator cataloguing river-crossing as a common NDE trope, and an audience member's question about the river
note: 6 of the 14 true positives are the same two accounts duplicated across channels

best_quote.text: beyond the field was a small river about 30 feet across. We came to the bank of the river and on the opposite bank gathered in a big group were all my loved ones who had passed away.

failure_modes: the circulating 'if you're white and you're in a white room, how would you know you're white?' teaching analogy about why souls incarnate - 5 passages, none of them a perceived place
